title: Pro-etale closed-support triangle before constructible restriction
statement:
Let $T$ be Noetherian, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a
closed immersion, and
let $j$ be its open complement. For a finite ring $A$, let
$Ri^!$ denote the right adjoint of the
direct image $i_*$ on the
pro-etale sites, taken on
the ambient ordinary derived categories, and let $Rj_*$ and $j^*$
be the direct image and the
inverse image of the open immersion $j$. In addition to the
open–closed triangle,
one has

$$
i_*Ri^!K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow Rj_*j^*K
\longrightarrow i_*Ri^!K[1]
\qquad(K\in D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)).
$$

No constructibility of $Ri^!K$ is part of this assertion.

proof.text: Work on the small skeletons and in the common sheaf universe of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For the finite ring $A$, use the sheaf of rings $A_S$ and left module sheaves of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], for $S=T,U,Z$; no commutativity of $A$ is needed. By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] these abelian categories are Grothendieck. Apply [lem-pur-kinjective-degreewise-existence] to a complex representing $K$ to choose a quasi-isomorphism $K\to I$ with $I$ K-injective and every $I^q$ injective. Use the exact inverse images with transported coefficient actions of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. Define an additive sheaf functor $H$ on left $A_T$-modules by $H(N)=i^*\ker(N\to j_*j^*N)$, using the open adjunction unit, and on morphisms by the induced kernel map followed by $i^*$. Kernels here are the sectionwise kernels of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Applying $H$ termwise preserves shifts and mapping-cone matrices, so its composite with derived localization is exact on homotopy categories. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived], its total right derived functor $RH$ exists and $RH(K)$ is represented by $H(I)$. Step 6 proves that $RH$ is the right adjoint $Ri^!$ in the statement and identifies its counit. No adjunction for $H$ has been assumed here.

source.place: ## Proof, choosing a K-injective resolution with injective terms and computing the closed right adjoint

proof.text: The geometric clause (1) of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], applied with auxiliary coefficient ring $\mathbf Z$, identifies $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with $T_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$. On an object $W\to U$, the inverse-image indexing category of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] has initial object $(W,W\to U\times_TW)$: the arrow from it to $(V,\phi)$ is forced to be the second component of $\phi$. The opposite category therefore has a final object, and the inverse-image colimit is $N(W)$. Restriction is already a sheaf, since localized coverings are the same coverings. This calculation applies also to rings and their actions. For the coefficient sheaves of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], restriction to the localized site gives the same presheaf $W\mapsto\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0(|W|),A)$ before sheafification. The canonical coefficient map of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] is thus the identity under this identification: both maps send a constant $a$ to $a$, and on each open fibre of a locally constant function the two maps agree, hence agree after gluing and sheafification. Consequently the module $j^*$ of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] is precisely restriction, including its action and its unit. It preserves quasi-isomorphisms by exactness. By [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized], $j^*I$ is K-injective, so it resolves $j^*K$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] to the termwise additive functor $j_*$ followed by derived localization: it preserves shifts and cone matrices (identities, differentials and their negatives), hence defines an exact functor on homotopy categories. Thus $Rj_*j^*K$ is represented by $j_*j^*I$. On an object $V\to T$, this complex has terms $I^q(V_U)$, $V_U=V\times_TU$, and the unit is restriction $I^q(V)\to I^q(V_U)$ by the direct-image formula in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For completeness, the derived unit is indeed this termwise unit: because $j^*$ is exact and left adjoint to $j_*$, [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] makes $j_*J$ K-injective whenever $J$ is K-injective on $U$. For any complex $M$, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] and the termwise adjunction, which respects differentials and homotopies, give $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(U)}(j^*M,QJ)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K(U)}(j^*M,J)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K(T)}(M,j_*J)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(T)}(QM,Qj_*J)$. Here $Q$ denotes localization and $K(S)$ the homotopy category on $S$. With $M=I$ and $J=j^*I$, the identity on $j^*I$ corresponds to precisely $I\to j_*j^*I$, so the represented map is the derived open unit.

source.place: ## Proof, exact open restriction, K-injectivity, and the computation of Rj_*

proof.text: For an object $V$ of $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$, put $V_U=V\times_TU$ and let $a:V_U\to V$ be the open inclusion. It is a monomorphism by clause (4) of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], again using auxiliary ring $\mathbf Z$ for the geometric assertion. Let $P_V=A_T[h_V]$ be the free module presheaf of [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module] and $L_V=P_V^\#$ its module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. The map $P_{V_U}\to P_V$ sends $e_b$ to $e_{ab}$ at an object $W$. It commutes with restriction because both composites send $r e_b$ to $r|_c e_{abc}$. Since $a$ is monic, the basis map $\operatorname{Hom}(W,V_U)\to\operatorname{Hom}(W,V)$ is injective. A free-module element in its kernel has every coefficient zero, so the presheaf map is componentwise injective, hence monic. Exact module sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-sheafification-exact] gives a monomorphism $L_{V_U}\to L_V$.

source.place: ## Proof, the monomorphism of free module sheaves for the open part

proof.text: The free-presheaf bijection [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module] and the sheafification adjunction [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] give $\operatorname{Hom}(L_V,N)=N(V)$. Precomposing with $L_{V_U}\to L_V$ corresponds to restriction: the map associated to $x\in N(V)$ sends $e_b$ to $x|_b$, so on the identity generator of $V_U$ its precomposition has value $x|_a$. For $y\in I^q(V_U)$ extend the corresponding $L_{V_U}\to I^q$ across the monomorphism of Step 3, using injectivity in the precise sense of [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. The extension corresponds to $x\in I^q(V)$ with $x|_a=y$. Hence $I^q\to j_*j^*I^q$ is sectionwise surjective for every site object $V$. It is epic: two sheaf maps out of its target agreeing after it agree on every section by such lifts, and hence are equal by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: ## Proof, injectivity extends sections and proves the termwise surjectivity

proof.text:
Put $F^q=\ker(\eta^q:I^q\to j_*j^*I^q)$; these kernels are sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. On an object $W\to U$, the restriction unit is the identity under $W\times_TU=W$, so $F^q(W)=0$ and $j^*F^q=0$. The open complement is quasi-compact as a morphism. Indeed, [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal] applied to complements in $T$ of finite unions from an open cover of any open subset $O\subseteq T$ supplies a maximal such finite union. Adjoining any further member cannot enlarge it, so it equals $O$. Thus every open subset of $T$ is quasi-compact, in particular $U\cap V$ for every affine open $V\subseteq T$; this is the required quasi-compactness of $j$. The current statement of [lem-exc-proetale-closed-essential-image] is for commutative ring-sheaf coefficients, so apply it after the following elementary restriction of scalars, rather than directly to $A_T$. Since $A$ is finite, $1_A$ has a positive additive order $n$; put $B=\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$. Integer multiples of $1_A$ give a central ring map $B\to A$ and therefore, on the continuous-function presheaves of Step 1 and by sheafification, maps $B_S\to A_S$ for $S=T,Z,U$. The structure maps for $B$ and $A$ in [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] commute with these maps: both composites send each constant integer residue to that multiple of $1_A$, and agreement on open fibres extends by gluing and sheafification. By the transported-action formula of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact], forgetting from $A_S$-modules to $B_S$-modules thus commutes with $i^*,j^*,i_*$ and their underlying unit maps. In particular, for any $A_T$-module $N$ with $j^*N=0$, the cited essential-image node applied to the commutative coefficient sheaf $B_T$ and its canonical inverse-image identifications gives an invertible underlying unit $\eta_N:N\to i_*i^*N$. This is the actual $A_T$-module unit: naturality of the inverse-image unit of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] with respect to the action map gives $\eta_N(rm)=\eta_{A_T}(r)\eta_N(m)$, and the direct-image coefficient action through $\rho_A=i_*c_i\circ\eta_{A_T}$ turns the right side into $r\eta_N(m)$. Its inverse $h$ is also $A_T$-linear, since $\eta_N(h(ry))=ry=\eta_N(rh(y))$ and $\eta_N$ is injective. The same restriction of scalars shows $j^*i_*M=0$ for every $A_Z$-module $M$, by the other direction of the essential-image node. No commutativity of $A$ was used. Apply this supported-unit conclusion to $N=F^q$ to obtain the canonical $A_T$-linear unit isomorphism $F^q\to i_*i^*F^q=i_*HI^q$. Use its inverse to obtain the kernel inclusion $i_*HI^q\to I^q$. Naturality of $\eta$ gives $\eta^{q+1}d_I^q=(j_*j^*d_I^q)\eta^q$, so $d_I^q$ restricts to $F^q\to F^{q+1}$; its square is zero by cancellation of the kernel inclusion. Naturality of the closed unit makes the displayed identification of $F$ with $i_*HI$ an identification of complexes. The kernel inclusions and the units are complex maps, and Step 4 makes the units epic. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-cochain-complexes-degreewise-exact] gives the short exact sequence of complexes
$$0\longrightarrow i_*HI\longrightarrow I\longrightarrow j_*j^*I\longrightarrow0.$$

source.place: ## Proof, identification of the supported kernel and assembly of the short exact complex sequence

proof.text:
The quasi-compact-complement condition verified in Step 5 allows [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact], so $i_*$ is exact for the given finite ring $A$. The supported kernel construction of Step 5 is a sheaf right adjoint to $i_*$. Indeed $j^*i_*M=0$ for every left $A_Z$-module $M$ by that step. Naturality of the open unit therefore makes every map $i_*M\to N$ factor uniquely through $F(N)=\ker(N\to j_*j^*N)$. The supported unit isomorphism $F(N)\xrightarrow{\sim}i_*i^*F(N)=i_*H(N)$ and full faithfulness of $i_*$ from [lem-exc-proetale-closed-fully-faithful] give natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_T(i_*M,N)=\operatorname{Hom}_T(i_*M,F(N))=\operatorname{Hom}_Z(M,H(N))$. The identity of $H(N)$ corresponds to the inverse supported-unit isomorphism followed by the kernel inclusion into $N$. This is exactly the first map used in Step 5. The bijections are additive; applied in every degree, their naturality identifies chain maps and homotopies. Since the left adjoint $i_*$ is exact, [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] shows $H(I)$ is K-injective. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], for every complex $M$ on $Z$ there are natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(T)}(Qi_*M,QI)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K(T)}(i_*M,I)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K(Z)}(M,H(I))=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Z)}(QM,QH(I)).$$
Together with the functorial K-injective replacements and total-derived computation of Step 1, these identify $RH$ with the right adjoint $Ri^!$ on the entire unbounded derived categories. Taking $M=H(I)$ shows that the derived counit is the localization of the supported kernel inclusion of Step 5. Exactness of $i_*$ also means its termwise application computes the functor on derived categories: exactness identifies its cohomology with $i_*$ of cohomology, so it preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Thus $i_*H(I)$ represents $i_*Ri^!K$. Now apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] to the short exact sequence of Step 5. The middle and third terms represent $K$ and $Rj_*j^*K$ by Steps 1 and 2; its first two arrows have just been identified as the exceptional counit and the open unit. It gives precisely
$$i_*Ri^!K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow Rj_*j^*K\longrightarrow i_*Ri^!K[1].$$
No step assumes constructibility or boundedness of $K$ or of $Ri^!K$.
